alex: ran an nsys capture on the repro batch — seeing host->device memcpy on stream 0 serializing a supposedly higher-priority compute stream. attaching qdrep. anyone seen memcpy block kernels like this? @maria @jonathan

maria: can you paste the nsys command you used and confirm if host buffers were page-locked? cudaMemcpyAsync will fall back to sync if memory isn't pinned. :thinking:

alex: command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn -o run1 --capture-range=none ./serving_perf_test --workload=batch=32
```
I was using numpy -> torch.frombuffer -> .cuda() path (no explicit pin). attaching run1.qdrep link.

jonathan: that plumbing will allocate regular host memory; cudaMemcpyAsync becomes synchronous under the hood. two quick checks: 1) switch to pinned host buffers (torch.tensor(..., pin_memory=True)) and 2) use explicit cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated stream with cudaStreamCreateWithPriority. also confirm you're not implicitly synchronizing with default stream semantics.

sam: fwiw the timeline also shows short CPU scheduling gaps around the copy events (~20-40ms). process gets preempted and the memcpy spans that preemption which makes the hostcopy look long — could be python GC or aio thread churn. try pinning the process to a CPU core (numactl -C) and re-run.

alex: noted. i'll try pin_memory + explicit async copies + cpu pinning. quick question: is there any nsys flag to better distinguish cudaMemcpyAsync fallback vs true async? or markers to show if host memory is pinned?

maria: nsys doesn't label "pinned" but the timing pattern is telling: if a copy shows up on host timeline and CPU thread is doing heavy work concurrently, it often means pageable fallback. also check driver logs; cudart may show warnings in debug builds. alternatively, use cudaHostRegister on the buffer and see if memcpy latency drops.

jonathan: another trick: run with cudaMemcpyAsync + cudaStreamSynchronize on the stream after the call to test if the memcpy was async. if latency doesn't change it's likely async; if it forces sync it will reveal fallback. low-effort: replace the path with a pinned allocation and compare baseline.

sam: for the CPU-preemptions, record perf sched on the worker process or enable perfetto scheduling track in nsys (--trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt?) to capture more OS-level events. i had similar surprises where kafka consumer threads spiked GC and killed steady copy throughput.

alex: thanks all — rerunning now with pin_memory + explicit stream async copies and numactl pin. i'll post updated trace. deploy-bot: run1.qdrep uploaded to s3://redwood-traces/1918765432-run1.qdrep :white_check_mark:
